name: Community Accelerator Grant
award: $2,500 to $25,000 unrestricted; $10 million pool (2026)
opens: 2026 cycle opened July 15, 2026; 2027 window expected mid-July
notes: Unrestricted general operating grants to Washington arts and culture nonprofits, fiscally sponsored groups and tribal entities whose primary mission is producing or supporting arts and culture, established on or before Dec 31, 2022, with average annual budgets between $25,000 and $1 million (FY2023-FY2025). For-profits, government entities (other than tribes) and churches are not eligible. Prioritizes BIPOC, LGBTQ+, disabled and rural-led organizations. Pattern: info session early July, application open mid-July to late August, notification by Dec 1, funds by Dec 31.

name: Creative Equity Fund
funder: ArtsFund (with City of Seattle Office of Arts & Culture, Seattle Foundation, Satterberg Foundation and others)
award: $70,000 per year for three years ($210,000 total) to three grantees
opens: 2026 round opened May 26, 2026
notes: Multi-year unrestricted funding for King County arts and culture organizations that are BIPOC, LGBTQ+ or disability-led (50%+ of staff or board), founded on or before Dec 31, 2021, with average budgets of $50,000 to $500,000. ArtsFund states there are no plans for another round after 2026, so treat this as closed unless re-announced.

name: Annual Allocations (Cultural Partners general operating grants)
award: Varies; $2.48 million distributed to 58 organizations in a recent cycle
opens: Invitations emailed mid-December; past deadlines late February
notes: Invitation-only general operating support for arts and culture nonprofits with at least three years of continuous operation in King County (budget $200,000+) or Pierce County (budget $100,000+). Art festivals running fewer than 10 days, historic preservation, children's museums and individual artists are excluded. Contact ArtsFund staff to be considered for an invitation; dates not publicly posted.

name: Grants to Organizations: Art Project Grant (FY2027)
contact: Miguel Guillén, Grants to Organizations Program Manager, 360-753-3860; Ashley Marshall, Program Assistant
award: $1,000 to $3,000 (FY2027 requests); amounts vary with available funds

deadlines.label: FY2027 cycle (closed); FY2028 dates not yet posted

opens: FY2027 opened March 9, 2026; programs usually announced in January and open about six weeks between February and April
notes: One-year project support for public arts, heritage or culture projects in Washington taking place July 1 to June 30 of the fiscal year. Open to 501(c)(3)s, fiscally sponsored groups, designated Local Arts Agencies and tribal governments; for-profits and individuals are not eligible. Ongoing programs are not funded; first consideration goes to organizations with budgets of $0 to $50,000 and to applicants outside King County and the City of Tacoma. Reimbursement grant: reimbursement form due June 30, 2027, final report July 31, 2027. Requires WA UBI, UEI and Statewide Vendor number.

name: Grants to Organizations: General Operating Support (FY26-FY27 two-year; small, midsized and large tiers)
contact: Miguel Guillén, Grants to Organizations Program Manager, 360-753-3860; Ashley Marshall, Program Assistant
award: Midsized tier: up to $6,000 over two years ($3,000 per year); other tiers vary by budget size

deadlines.label: FY26-FY27 two-year cycle (closed); next two-year cycle (FY28-29) expected spring 2027

opens: FY26-27 opened March 3, 2025; next cycle expected to open around March 2027
notes: Two-year operating support for Washington organizations whose mission focuses on art, culture and/or heritage with at least three years of publicly accessible programming. Tiers by annual budget (midsized is $100,000 to $350,000). Eligible: 501(c)(3)s, fiscally sponsored groups, designated Local Arts Agencies and tribal governments; for-profits, religious organizations, schools and most government agencies are not. Priority for distressed counties and organizations with 25%+ underserved constituencies. Final reports due July 31, 2026 and July 31, 2027.

name: Grants to Organizations: Arts Service Organization Support
contact: Miguel Guillén, Grants to Organizations Program Manager, 360-753-3860; Ashley Marshall, Program Assistant
award: Not published for FY27; two-year grants
opens: Two-year cycle; FY26-27 round closed in spring 2025, next expected spring 2027
notes: Two-year support limited to regional and statewide arts service organizations that provide services to the arts field (not event producers themselves). Reimbursement-based like all GTO grants. Watch the ArtsWA newsletter for the FY28-29 announcement.

name: Creative Districts Capital Projects (CDCP) Grant FY26-27
contact: ArtsWA Creative Districts program (request forms by email); 360-753-3860
award: Up to $50,000 per community; $445,000 pool

deadlines.label: FY26-27 cycle (closed); next biennial cycle expected fall 2027

opens: FY26-27 opened September 23, 2025
match: 100% match (cash or in-kind), reduced to 50% to 80% for communities below state median income; match must be secured before award
notes: Only administering organizations of Washington State Certified Creative Districts may apply (cities, nonprofits, special districts, tribes). Funds bricks-and-mortar projects such as stages, performance spaces, wayfinding, lighting and murals that benefit the public for at least five years. Reimbursement only, prevailing wage applies. Project work complete and final report due June 30, 2027.

name: Tribal Cultural Grant
funder: Washington State Arts Commission (ArtsWA) Tribal Cultural Affairs Program
contact: Cheryl Wilcox, 360-485-1278, cheryl.wilcox@arts.wa.gov; Todd Clark, 360-485-1223, todd.clark@arts.wa.gov
award: About $18,000 per tribe (non-competitive, if all 29 federally recognized tribes apply); additional requests considered

deadlines.label: FY2026 cycle (closed); FY2027 dates not yet posted

opens: FY2026 opened February 4, 2025; next cycle expected to open early February
notes: Non-competitive formula funding for Washington's federally recognized tribes for tribal cultural activities as the tribe defines them (language, foodways, regalia, cultural events, tribal museums). One application per tribe per year. Spending period July 1 to June 30. Only tribes may apply.

name: Opportunity Grants
award: Up to $1,000 (per most recent published guidelines); no match required
opens: Ongoing; apply at least eight weeks before the event
notes: Small grants for public humanities presentations and events (talks, panels, discussions, festival humanities programming) open to the general public. Applicant must be a nonprofit or public agency organized in Washington; incorporation and tax-exempt status not required but the group must be organized for nonprofit purposes; individuals ineligible. Each project must involve at least one humanities scholar and conclude within one year. Prior grantees must file a final report before reapplying. Confirm the current cap on humanities.org since the program guidelines are updated periodically.

name: Spark Grants
award: Not confirmed in this research; larger than Opportunity Grants (verify on humanities.org)
opens: Not confirmed
notes: Humanities Washington's larger project grant for public humanities programming (community conversations, exhibits, lecture series, cultural festivals with humanities content). Same general eligibility as Opportunity Grants (Washington nonprofits and public agencies, scholar involvement). The program page could not be retrieved during this research, so amounts and the 2027 deadline must be verified directly with Humanities Washington.

name: Washington Stories Fund
award: $2,500 to $7,500; up to five grants per state region (Central, Central Puget Sound, Eastern, Northwestern, Southwestern)
opens: 2025 cycle closed; 2026/2027 dates not posted
notes: Funds projects that record and share little-known stories of people and groups who contributed to Washington's cultural richness (oral histories, documentaries, exhibits, storytelling events). Any nonprofit organization, public agency or group organized for nonprofit purposes may apply; individuals cannot. Awards are distributed regionally so rural applicants compete within their own region.

name: SWT Grant Programs (Rural Tourism Marketing and Production, Sports Incentivization, Arts and Culture, Tourism Regeneration, Technical Assistance, Sustainability)
award: Historically up to $50,000 (Rural Marketing and Production, Tourism Regeneration), $30,000 (Sports Incentivization, Arts and Culture, Sustainability), $15,000 (Technical Assistance)

deadlines.label: Rural Tourism Marketing and Production 2024-25 cycle (closed); SWT states no grant programs will be offered in 2026

opens: Not offered in 2026; EDA pandemic-recovery funding has ended
match: Match strongly encouraged but not required (prior cycles)
notes: SWT's grant suite (local governments, tribes, chambers, DMOs and tourism nonprofits) was funded by a federal EDA pass-through via Commerce and all programs are now marked closed; SWT says it will not offer grants in 2026. Sports Incentivization and Arts and Culture grants previously supported events that drew overnight visitors. Monitor the SWT industry site for any new state-funded round. SWT also runs paid co-op marketing programs for partners (not grants).

name: Building for the Arts (2027-29 biennium)
award: Up to $2,000,000 per project; $18,000,000 requested pool

deadlines.label: 2027-29 biennium application (closed); next biennium (2029-31) expected summer 2028

opens: 2027-29 applications accepted spring 2026 via ZoomGrants
match: State grant covers up to 33% of eligible capital costs; applicant funds the remainder through an active capital campaign
notes: Capital grants for acquisition, construction and major renovation of arts and cultural facilities (performing arts, art museums, cultural organizations). Applicants must be federally recognized tribes or Washington nonprofits with site control (ownership or 15-year recorded lease), LEED commitment, prevailing wage compliance and demonstrated capital campaign progress. Awards depend on legislative appropriation in the 2027-29 capital budget.

name: Heritage Capital Projects Grant
award: Not published in this research; biennial capital awards tied to the state capital budget
opens: Biennial; applications open February 1 of even-numbered years with two-stage submission (eligibility stage in spring, full plans in early summer)
notes: Capital funding for construction, rehabilitation or acquisition of facilities and landscapes that provide public access to Washington history (museums, historic venues, interpretive sites). Eligible: nonprofits, local governments, tribes and public development authorities. Applications go through the Washington Heritage Portal. The 2027-29 cycle would have run spring 2026; confirm status and the 2029-31 timeline with WSHS.

name: Valerie Sivinski Fund
award: Up to $3,000 per application
opens: Applications typically open late summer; notification by end of December
notes: Small grants for community-level historic preservation in Washington, including public education and interpretive programs and events about a specific historic or cultural resource. Applicants must be Washington Trust members at the nonprofit level or above; eligible applicants include nonprofits, unincorporated citizen groups, public agencies, school districts, civic and religious organizations. Projects must finish within one year; no general operating or expenses before January 1 of the award year.

name: Tourism Marketing Support Program (2026-2027)
award: Up to $20,000 per awardee (Tier 1) or $10,000 (Tier 2); $600,000 pool in 2024-25
opens: Usually announced December to January, due late February or early March
match: 2:1 (Port provides $2 for every $1 of applicant funds; up to 50% of match may be administrative costs in Tier 2)
notes: Funds out-of-state and international marketing of Washington destinations and events that use Port facilities (SEA Airport, cruise terminals, marinas). Eligible: chambers, DMOs, cities, counties, ports, tribes, nonprofit attractions and nonprofits producing events that attract out-of-state visitors. Festivals are regularly funded. Statewide, not limited to King County. For-profits cannot apply.
recent_recipients: Northwest Maritime Center Wooden Boat Festival $11,200 (2024-25)

name: Airport Community Ecology (ACE) Fund Small Matching Grants

geography.region: Airport-adjacent cities in south King County

award: Small matching grants (not verified in this research)
opens: Not verified
notes: Small matching grants for community-led environmental and community projects in the six cities near SEA Airport. Details could not be verified during this research (the Port's page was not reachable); confirm the current cycle, award cap and eligibility at portseattle.org before listing to users.

name: Grants for Arts Projects (GAP)
contact: arts.gov; discipline specialists listed in guidelines
award: $10,000 to $100,000 ($30,000 to $150,000 for Local Arts Agency subgranting)

deadlines.label: FY2027 GAP 1 Part 1 (closed; projects start Jan 1, 2027)
FY2027 GAP 2 Part 1 (closed; projects start June 1, 2027)

opens: FY2028 guidelines expected late 2026 with Part 1 deadlines in February and July 2027
notes: Federal project grants for nonprofits, units of state or local government and federally recognized tribes with at least five years of arts programming and $20,000+ in operating expenses in the most recent fiscal year. Festivals apply under the relevant discipline (Folk and Traditional Arts, Music, Presenting and Multidisciplinary Works, etc.). Fiscal-sponsored and for-profit applicants are ineligible; one application per year. Two-part submission via Grants.gov then the NEA Applicant Portal; Part 2 deadlines fall about two weeks after Part 1.

name: Challenge America
award: $10,000 fixed request
opens: FY2028 cycle expected with the GAP February 2027 and July 2027 deadlines
match: Minimum 1:1 non-federal cost share (at least $10,000); total project at least $20,000
notes: Small federal grants for organizations with operating budgets under $250,000 that project arts programming to underserved communities (by geography, ethnicity, economic status or disability). Requires five years of arts programming history. Applied through the GAP system by selecting the Challenge America discipline. Good fit for small rural festival producers.

name: Tulalip Cares Charitable Fund
contact: Tulalip Tribes Charitable Fund, Tulalip, WA (mailed applications)
award: Not published; no more than 50% of an organization's operating budget; typically non-recurring
opens: Applications accepted quarterly; postmark deadlines by quarter (check tulalipcares.org)
notes: Casino-funded grants to Washington 501(c)(3) organizations and accredited K-12 institutions for arts, music, community and cultural activities, pre-K education and youth athletics, with priority for Snohomish County. One grant per organization per 12 months; no travel, legal fees, memorials or endowments. Mailed signed application with financials, board list and IRS letter; notification within 90 days of the quarterly deadline, unfunded applicants are not notified. Recipient lists are published on tulaliptribes-nsn.gov.

name: Muckleshoot Charity Fund

geography.region: Washington State, emphasis on the Puget Sound region around Auburn

award: Most awards $1,500 to $5,000
opens: No deadlines; reviewed quarterly. Apply 3 to 6 months before a date-specific event
notes: Casino-profit grants to Washington-registered nonprofits (501(c)(3) or RCW 9.46.0920), public schools and government agencies in priority areas including Culture, Arts, Communities of Color, Native American programs and Civic/Community. One grant per 12 months; for-profits and individuals ineligible. Online application via GrantRequest; only funded applicants are notified. Eliav's Seattle Glow has had Muckleshoot Casino as a sponsor, which is a separate casino sponsorship channel.

name: Puyallup Tribe Charity Trust Board grants
contact: charitytrustboard@puyalluptribe-nsn.gov; (253) 382-6012; 5580 Pacific Hwy E, Suite F, Fife
award: Not published; quarterly rounds of roughly $200,000 to $690,000 across 19 to 54 organizations
opens: Applications due by end of business each quarter and reviewed the following month (Q4 2024 deadline was Sept 27, 2024)
notes: Charitable gaming proceeds distributed quarterly to 501(c)(3) nonprofits, with preference for projects in Pierce County that benefit tribal members. Submit a single PDF (typed form, 501(c)(3) letter, W-9, budget) by email, fax or mail; incomplete packets are disqualified. Specific quarterly dates are posted on the tribe's site each quarter.
recent_recipients: 54 local organizations shared $690,000+ in one recent quarter (puyalluptribe-nsn.gov)

name: Kalispel Charitable Fund
funder: Kalispel Tribe of Indians / Northern Quest
award: Not published; about $1 million donated annually

deadlines.label: Spring 2027 program and event support cycle

opens: Online form only (not Chrome-compatible); apply in the cycle before an April or October event
notes: Program and event support for Washington-registered nonprofits in Spokane and Pend Oreille counties in education, health care, arts and culture, social services and environment. One comprehensive application per 12-month period (Oct 1 to Sept 30); auction items require 90 days notice. Teams, individuals and third-party requests are not accepted.

name: Snoqualmie Tribe nonprofit grants

geography.region: Washington State; about 90% of funds go to King County and Snoqualmie Valley organizations

award: Up to $50,000 (shared across one or more nonprofits in the 2024 round)

deadlines.label: 2026 window (closed; pattern is Jan 1 to Mar 31 annually)
Expected 2027 window close (pattern, not yet posted)

opens: Expected January 1, 2027
notes: Annual charitable grants to Washington 501(c)(3)s in categories including arts and culture, Snoqualmie Valley community services, environmental education, family, senior and veteran services. Applications accepted January 1 to March 31 with funding beginning in July. The tribe has also funded arts and sports organizations. Confirm the 2027 window on the tribe's donations site; the 2027 date above is the established pattern.

name: Community Impact Funds
contact: Swinomish Tribe, 11404 Moorage Way, La Conner, WA 98257
award: Not published
opens: Downloadable application; due annually April 14
notes: Annual Senate-approved awards to organizations operating in Washington in arts and culture, education and youth, environment, health care, public safety and social services. One award per organization per year; no political groups, memorials, endowments, travel or legal fees. Return the completed application with required attachments by April 14 at 6 p.m.

name: Appendix X Non-Profit Grants

geography.region: Kitsap County and the greater Puget Sound area

award: Not published; over 250 organizations supported annually across Suquamish giving programs
opens: Rolling online application at grantinterface.com; awards usually within 60 days of each quarterly deadline
notes: Compact-mandated grants for charitable, nonprofit and tribal community programs, with priority for youth services, education, health and wellness and environmental preservation. Quarterly deadlines Dec 31, Mar 31, Jun 30 and Sep 30. Organizations denied here may then apply to the PME Fund.

name: PME Fund (Port Madison Enterprises Board donations and sponsorships)

geography.region: Kitsap and Mason counties and Suquamish homelands

award: Not published
opens: Fillable PDF application by email or mail; quarterly review tied to event date
notes: Non-casino funds for donations and event sponsorships in the region. Applicants eligible for the Suquamish Appendix X fund must apply there first and may apply to PME if denied. Sponsorship and donation requests have separate requirements. The casino also offers in-kind donations with 4 to 6 weeks notice and a PME CEO Fund with one-month lead time.

name: Nisqually Tribe Charitable Fund
contact: Nisqually Indian Tribe, 4820 She-Nah-Num Dr SE, Olympia; contact form at nisqually-nsn.gov/contact

geography.region: South Puget Sound (Thurston and Pierce counties area); specific service area not published

award: Not published; annual recipient lists posted 2016-2025

deadlines.label: 2026 Charitable Application and Local Government Application (closed); 2027 date not yet posted

opens: Application materials posted on the tribe's charitable funds page, typically spring; due July 31
notes: Annual charitable contributions from the Nisqually Tribe with separate applications for nonprofits and local governments. The 2026 deadline was July 31, 2026; expect a similar mid-year deadline in 2027. Eligibility and amounts are described in the application packet rather than on the web page.

name: Yakama Cares Charitable Contributions Fund
award: Not published per grant; several hundred thousand dollars to over $1 million distributed annually to 100+ organizations

deadlines.label: 2025 cycle (closed); 2026 cycle followed the same March pattern; 2027 not yet posted

opens: Applications open early March, due March 31, awards distributed in May
notes: Annual grant round from Legends Casino Hotel for nonprofits within 100 miles of Toppenish, with priority for youth and education, elder care and medical needs; tribal nonprofits are not eligible. Public safety agencies and community groups are regularly funded. Apply through the Yakama Cares page on legendscasino.com.

name: Cowlitz Tribal Foundation: Clark County Fund
award: Not published

deadlines.label: 2026 Clark County Fund (closed); 2027 not yet posted

opens: 2026 round opened in spring; notification June 12, 2026
notes: Grants to 501(c)(3)s and fiscally sponsored community organizations serving Clark County. Annual cycle with a May 1 deadline in 2026. Watch the tribe's Submittable portal for the 2027 opening.

name: Cowlitz Tribal Foundation: Statewide Fund
award: Not published
opens: 2026 round open spring to June 30; 2027 not yet posted
notes: Statewide companion to the Clark County Fund for Washington nonprofits outside Clark County. 2026 deadline was June 30, 2026 with awards by late October. Expect a similar late-spring deadline in 2027.

name: Boeing Washington State community grants and community sponsorships
contact: Leah Hausman, leah.s.hausman@boeing.com (community sponsorships, economic mobility)
award: Not published; invitation-only grants plus a small number of larger community sponsorships
opens: Grant period opens around March 1 by invitation; event sponsorship requests must be emailed at least six months before the event
notes: Grantmaking is invitation-only in three pillars (STEM, veterans, economic mobility and environment); unsolicited proposals are not accepted. Separate community sponsorships may include arts and civic events, and event sponsorships are considered for nonprofits aligned with the pillars, typically with a Boeing executive on the board. Contact the local community investor first.

name: Costco Wholesale Charitable Contributions (warehouse donations and grants)
contact: Benevity online form (grants); warehouse donation request PDF
award: Not published
opens: Rolling, one request per fiscal year (Sept to Aug)
notes: Monetary requests only from 501(c)(3)s focused on children, education and health and human services in communities with a Costco warehouse. Local events apply through the warehouse donation form; larger broad-based organizations use the Benevity grant application. Arts and tourism events fit only if framed around children or education.

name: PSE Powerful Partnerships

geography.region: PSE electric and gas service territory

award: $12,500 contribution plus outreach partnership
opens: 2027 application round opens January 4, 2027
notes: Annual partnership (not a pure grant) with nonprofits in PSE's service territory that reach underserved residential customers; partners host six or more PSE outreach engagements and share energy-savings content. Suits community festivals and cultural events with large public attendance. The 2027 round opens January 4, 2027; closing date not posted.

name: PSE Foundation community grants
award: Varies; roughly $1.3 million across 550+ grants in a recent year
opens: Emergency and disaster relief category: apply by April 20 (year not stated); general cycle dates not posted
notes: Washington nonprofit grants focused on human services, food security, housing, emergency preparedness and education. Events are not a stated priority; relevant mainly for community events with a safety or resilience angle. Verify the current open window on psefoundation.org.

name: Avista Foundation grants (Arts and Culture, Economic and Community Vitality)

geography.region: Avista Utilities service territory in eastern and south-central Washington

award: Not published; 2024 grants totaled more than $500,000 across 150+ awards
opens: Applications accepted every three months; specific quarterly dates posted on avistafoundation.com
notes: Quarterly competitive grants in five areas including arts and culture and economic and community vitality for nonprofits in communities served by Avista Utilities (WA, ID, OR, MT) and Juneau. Take the online eligibility quiz before applying. Festival and cultural event producers in the Spokane region are regular recipients.

name: T-Mobile Hometown Grants
funder: T-Mobile (with Main Street America and Smart Growth America)
award: Up to $50,000 per town

deadlines.label: Q4 2026 portal close (quarterly: last day of each quarter)

opens: Portal reopens the first day of each quarter
notes: Funds shovel-ready physical projects that build or refresh community gathering spaces (parks, trails, downtown assets, historic buildings) in small towns, completed within 12 months. Applicants are local officials, tribal leaders or nonprofit community leaders. Not for operating costs or fees. The original five-year commitment has been described in the past tense, so confirm the program is still accepting applications before relying on it.

name: Kaiser Permanente Washington community sponsorships
funder: Kaiser Foundation Health Plan of Washington

geography.region: Washington counties served by Kaiser Permanente Washington (excludes Clark and Cowlitz, which fall under KP Northwest)

award: Not published
opens: Rolling quarterly sponsorship cycles; 2027 deadlines not yet posted (pattern: late January for May-July events, late May for Aug-Oct events, late August for Nov-Jan events, mid-October for Feb-Apr events)
notes: Sponsorships for community events and activities aligned with KP's community health needs assessment, evaluated on reach, brand exposure, equity and employee engagement. Community health grants are invitation-only. One sponsorship per organization per calendar year; no local sports teams, school events or endowments.

name: People Helping People Awards

geography.region: BECU membership areas (Washington; also OR, ID, SC)

award: $15,000 Community Benefit awards (14) up to $50,000 top award; plus $2,500 glide-path grants for two years
opens: Member nominations open early April; finalists voted on by members; winners announced in December
notes: Member-nominated (not open application) awards for 501(c)(3)s in education, economic opportunity, health, environment, basic needs and community strengthening. A BECU member must nominate the organization. Low fit for pure arts or tourism events.

name: Strategic Project Grants

geography.region: Pacific Northwest (WA, OR, ID, MT, AK)

award: Varies; typically larger capacity, capital and program-expansion grants
opens: Eligibility quiz then LOI during posted windows (fall and spring); invited full applications; decisions roughly six months later
notes: Capacity-building grants for construction, renovation, equipment and new staff or program expansion at Pacific Northwest nonprofits including arts and culture organizations. Not for annual events or operating. Three-stage process with capped LOI windows; declined applicants wait one year, returning grantees three years. Check murdocktrust.org for the fall 2026 and spring 2027 LOI windows.

name: Neighbor to Neighbor (N2N) grants

geography.region: South Seattle, White Center and Kent

award: Up to $7,500 (recent grantees received $8,500)

deadlines.label: Quarterly deadline (Oct 30); summer 2026 cycle was paused

opens: Quarterly; the summer 2026 cycle was paused and the application was expected to reopen in fall 2026
notes: Grassroots grants for resident-led groups (budgets generally under $200,000) in South Seattle, White Center and Kent that address economic and racial disparities, including community festivals and cultural gatherings. 501(c)(3) or fiscal sponsor required; one grant per calendar year; contact the program consultant before applying. Confirm the cycle has resumed before counting on a date.

name: The Morgan Fund performing arts grants (2026-2027 cycle)
award: Project grants up to $40,000; general operating up to $30,000 (invitation only)
opens: Annual; next cycle expected summer 2027
notes: Supports dance and theatre nonprofits in the Puget Sound region (or Washington, DC) with project grants for productions, capital equipment and capacity. One application per organization per cycle. Not for festivals outside dance and theatre.

name: Norman Archibald Charitable Foundation
funder: Norman Archibald Charitable Foundation (administered by Seattle Foundation)
award: Not published
opens: Rolling; proposals reviewed at quarterly board meetings
notes: Supports 501(c)(3)s operating in Northwest Washington with priority for capital and equipment projects. Arts and youth-arts organizations in King and Pierce counties are referred to ArtsFund; school foundations are ineligible. Useful for event infrastructure purchases rather than event operations.

name: Whitehorse Foundation
award: Not published
opens: Two-page letters of inquiry accepted on an ongoing basis and reviewed after each quarter
notes: Funds Snohomish County nonprofits serving children, youth and families. Two-step process: LOI, then invited full application. Youth-focused festivals or family events are the fit.

name: Benjamin N. Phillips Memorial Fund
award: Not published

deadlines.label: 2026 letter of inquiry (closed); full applications were due Sept 30, 2026

opens: LOIs open July 6, due August 7; invitations Sept 3; applications due Sept 30 (annual pattern)
notes: Charitable organizations serving Clallam County. Two-step annual process each summer. Expect a similar July to September schedule in 2027.

name: Community Grants Program

geography.region: Eastern Washington (10 counties) and North Idaho

award: $2,500 to $15,000; more than $1 million awarded annually

deadlines.label: 2026 final (closed); 2027 round expected to open December 2026

opens: Round typically announced mid-December with early-bird deadline in early January and final deadline in early February
notes: Annual competitive grants in arts and culture, economic opportunity, education and youth, health and quality of life for 501(c)(3)s, tribes, public entities and unincorporated associations serving the 20-county region. One application per cycle; early-bird applicants enter a $1,000 operating grant drawing. 2026 theme was Building Stability and Belonging.

name: Longest Table Microgrants

geography.region: Eastern Washington and North Idaho (20 counties)

award: Up to $2,500 per event; goal of at least 60 events funded

deadlines.label: 2026 applications opened Apr 17; reviewed on a rolling basis from May 5 until funds ran out

opens: Expected to reopen spring 2027 for events June 1 to September 30
notes: Microgrants for community-led Longest Table shared-meal events (tables, chairs, permits, promotion, youth activities). Open to 501(c)(3)s, tribes, public entities and unincorporated groups in the Innovia region. Rolling review until funds are exhausted, so apply as soon as the window opens.

name: Woods Family Music and Arts Grant
funder: Community Foundation of North Central Washington

geography.region: Chelan, Douglas and Okanogan counties (excluding the Methow Valley)

award: Up to $5,000
opens: Applications open in August each year
notes: Project or operating support for music and arts programming in Chelan, Douglas and Okanogan counties (Methow Valley excluded). Open to 501(c)(3)s, government entities including schools, religious organizations and fiscally sponsored groups; one application per organization per cycle. Funds must be spent within one year; projects completed before award are ineligible.

name: Upper Valley Fund grants
funder: Community Foundation of North Central Washington
award: Grants of about $2,000 and up (listing inconsistent; confirm with CFNCW)
opens: Annual cycle; dates posted on cfncw.org
notes: Geographic community fund for 501(c)(3)s serving Leavenworth, Dryden, Peshastin, Lake Wenatchee and Plain; government and faith-based groups eligible only for project-specific requests; public schools ineligible. Relevant to Leavenworth festival planning. CFNCW also runs similar legacy and community funds (Cashmere, Waterville, Methow, Grand Coulee) with their own cycles.

name: Project Neighborly grants
award: Up to $5,000; $173,000 to 36 projects in 2024
opens: Typically announced in spring; 2026/2027 dates not posted
notes: Funds ideas that bring neighbors together across differences (block parties, cultural gatherings, community meals, festivals) anywhere in Whatcom County. Open to nonprofits, tribal agencies, public and religious institutions and fiscally sponsored community groups such as granges and neighborhood associations. Check whatcomcf.org for the next round.

name: Community Grants
funder: The Community Foundation of South Puget Sound
award: Typically $1,500 to $7,500; about $400,000 total in 2025, intended as two years of funding

deadlines.label: 2025 cycle (closed); foundation states Community Grants reopen in 2027

opens: Expected to reopen August 2027 (2025 opened Aug 4, due Aug 29)
notes: Mostly unrestricted grants to 501(c)(3)s and fiscally sponsored groups with at least three board members, used entirely within Thurston, Mason and Lewis counties, with arts and culture and civic engagement among the priorities. Two-year funding means no 2026 round; next opening is 2027. Service clubs, schools, PTOs and sports teams are ineligible.

name: Yakima Valley Sponsorship Grants
contact: Send a letter or email request to YVCF at least 60 days before the event

geography.region: Yakima Valley (Kittitas County eligible with limited funding)

award: Up to $3,000
opens: Rolling, subject to funding availability; request at least 60 days before the event
notes: Event and project sponsorships for 501(c)(3)s and government entities whose events benefit the Yakima Valley community. Submit a letter describing the organization, event, request amount and community benefit. No capital construction, endowments, lobbying or sectarian activity.

name: Discretionary Grants

geography.region: Walla Walla, Columbia and Garfield counties (plus Umatilla County, OR)

opens: Annual cycle; 2026/2027 dates not published in this research
notes: Grants to 501(c)(3)s, municipalities, tribal governments and fiscally sponsored groups serving the Blue Mountain region. Fundraising events and event sponsorships are explicitly excluded, so frame requests as programs or community projects, not galas. Expenses already incurred are ineligible.

name: Focus Grants
opens: 2026 round opened mid-July
notes: Larger grants aimed at reducing intergenerational poverty and building resilience among underserved families in Southwest Washington; cultural events qualify only when they serve those priority populations and are community-led. Open to nonprofits, fiscally sponsored projects, government and tribal agencies, churches and school districts.

name: Annual Grant Cycle
award: $500 to $10,000, average about $4,000; limited awards above $10,000 with staff pre-approval
opens: Applications typically open in August; 2027 expected similar
notes: Grants to 501(c)(3)s serving Benton and Franklin counties, one application per cycle. Fundraising events and sponsorships are not funded, but community events with direct public benefit may be considered. No capital, endowment or retroactive costs; schools, PTOs, service clubs and sports teams ineligible.

name: Community Grants Program

geography.region: Kitsap County and North Mason County

award: Up to $5,000
opens: Applications typically open late summer
notes: Program or operating grants to nonprofits serving Kitsap or North Mason County in arts and culture, youth, education, environment and health. Reviewed on validated need, other support, evaluation and community impact.

name: Annual Grant Cycle
award: No set minimum or maximum; average $7,000 to $12,000, past awards $500 to $35,000
opens: Opens November 1, 2026
notes: Competitive grants for nonprofits serving Skagit County in basic needs, arts and culture, youth and education. Up to two requests per cycle for different purposes; requests of $20,000 or more need reviewed or audited financials. The foundation also pays McIntyre Hall venue fees for local performing arts groups through designated funds.

name: Quarterly Impact Grants
award: Up to $5,000
opens: Quarterly; contact the foundation for the exact schedule
notes: Small quarterly grants for nonprofits serving Grays Harbor residents in the foundation's priority areas, which include arts, culture and history and community connection. Suited to one-time events, which the larger Community Building Grants exclude.

name: Community Building Grants
opens: Two cycles per year, due April 1 and October 1
notes: Larger project grants for charitable entities (501(c)(3)s, school districts, cities) serving the public in Grays Harbor County. One award per 12 months. Excludes ongoing operating support and one-time activities, so recurring festival infrastructure or program development fits better than a single event.

name: Rick Steves Europe Fund Capacity Grants
award: Up to $5,000
opens: 2027 not yet posted
notes: Capacity-building grants (fundraising, finance, leadership, sustainability) for nonprofits, school districts and public agencies serving Snohomish County, with priority for BIPOC, immigrant and refugee-led groups and budgets of $1 million or less. Not for event costs, but useful for a small festival organization's infrastructure.

name: Suquamish Clearwater Casino Resort donations and sponsorships
funder: Suquamish Clearwater Casino Resort (Port Madison Enterprises)
award: Goods, services and cash; amounts not published
opens: Submit 4 to 6 weeks before the donation is needed (requests with less than 4 weeks notice are not accepted); CEO Fund one week
notes: In-kind and cash donations to Washington-registered nonprofits and 501(c)(3)s, more likely approved for Kitsap County events. No cash to political groups or children's organizations. Only approved applicants receive a reply. Cash can come from either Casino Donations or the PME CEO Fund in a calendar year, not both.
